name: Dark hybrid vocal pad: choir-like wavetable plus an octave-up choir sample FM'd in (~34%), with sub and a little noise. Lows/mids are low-passed while the natural sample keeps the highs, a subtle LFO notch moves the mids, and one slow rising ramp drives the FX
goal: Build a dark, haunting vocal pad for intros, breakdowns or tension layers by blending a real choir sample with synthetic layers that sound vocal. Osc A: a choir-type wavetable with chorus-like unison and its position moved by a single slow, rising ramp (one main movement). Osc B: a choir multisample an octave up with light tube saturation, frequency-modulating A at ~34% for grit. Add a default sub (choir has little sub) and very low white noise (or hum) for full-spectrum air. Route A + sub through a low-pass, but keep B (natural) out of it so the high end comes from the real voice. Then all go into filter 2, a subtle notch (~18%) whose amount and cutoff move on the LFO for mid-range expression. FX: a blended, very wide frequency-shifter/blur stereo layer (mix ~half), dimension ~6%, hyper-chorus automated up to ~32% at the top of the ramp, ping-pong delay ~10–11%, distortion only above ~300 Hz, a little comb, reverb ~10%, then a high-end presence boost. Delta vs our pad skills: natural-highs / synthetic-lows routing and the single-ramp FX bloom on a vocal pad.

source.title: The Secret to HUGE Dark Vocal Pads in Serum 2
source.transcript_note: Preset walkthrough; factory content names omitted; pack promo dropped.

prerequisites: Wavetable synth with a choir-like table and a sample/multisample oscillator that can FM osc A (Web Audio: AudioBufferSource choir + oscillator with FM via GainNode to frequency, implementation note)
Sub and noise oscillators, two filters incl. notch
FX: frequency-shift/blur widener, chorus/dimension, ping-pong delay, high-passed distortion, comb, reverb, EQ

inputs.name: choir_sample
inputs.description: Original/licensed choir 'ah'/'oo' recording (no vendor factory content)

outputs.name: dark_vocal_pad
outputs.description: Cohesive dark choir pad with natural highs and synthetic low/mid power

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Use your own or licensed choir material; vendor wavetable/multisample names are omitted.
Most FX are very subtle (≈6–11% mixes); the character comes from stacking many small moves.
Distortion is applied above ~300 Hz only; full-band saturation gets muddy.
Percentages are the presenter's knob values; treat as starting points.

steps.action: Osc A: choir-like wavetable, unison for chorus, slight low-pass. Create one main modulator, a slow triangle that effectively ramps up, on wavetable position (and later FX amounts).
Osc B: choir multisample an octave higher with a bit of tube saturation, defaults otherwise. FM it into osc A at ~34% for a touch of grit.
Add a sub oscillator at default level under everything, and white noise (or hum) at a very low level for full-spectrum air.
steps.expect: Low-end weight and subtle high air

steps.action: Filter 1: low-pass on osc A + sub only; route osc B around it so the natural choir provides the high end.
steps.expect: Synthetic layers give low/mid power; natural sample keeps highs

steps.action: Filter 2 on the combined signal: notch at ~18% mix (100% shows the full effect), with the amount rising on the LFO and the cutoff moving slightly too, for mid-range expression and cohesion.

FX 1: a frequency-shifter/blur stereo layer, mix ~half, blur ~half, shift and range lowered, blended in as a moving super-wide layer. Dimension ~6%. Hyper-chorus automated from low up to ~32% at the top of the ramp.
steps.expect: Wide moving layer that turns phasey only at the peak

steps.action: FX 2: ping-pong delay ~10–11%; distortion with a high-pass so only ~300 Hz upward is saturated; a little comb filter (macro candidate); reverb ~10%; final high-shelf presence boost.

verification: Muting osc B removes most of the natural high end.
Notch at 18% is subtle; sweeping to 100% reveals the full notch.
Distortion leaves content below ~300 Hz clean.
Over a held chord, chorus/phasing increases toward the end of the ramp.
